headline: LION ONE ZONE 500 DELIVERS 44.39 G/T GOLD — First Underground Hole Into Feeder Zone Hits 2.0m of Ultra-High Grade at Tuvatu
snippet: Lion One Metals (TSXV: LIO) announced on November 25 that its first underground drill hole targeting Zone 500 at the Tuvatu Gold Mine in Fiji returned 2.0 metres at 44.39 g/t gold — intercepted 60 metres away from planned position, confirming the feeder zone extends further than previously modelled. For retail investors, an ultra-high-grade underground intercept in a confirmed feeder zone is the geological event that triggers resource model upgrades; at 44 g/t, even narrow widths are economic, and the miss-by-60m discovery implies the system remains open in multiple directions.

headline: CHINA GALLIUM/ANTIMONY/GERMANIUM BAN EXPIRES NOVEMBER 27 — No Extension Announced; Western Tech and Defence Supply Chains Exposed
snippet: China's suspension of its ban on gallium, germanium, and antimony exports to the United States is due to expire on November 27 — tomorrow — and as of November 25 no extension had been published, raising the prospect of an immediate reimposition that would cut off Western defence, semiconductor, and clean-energy supply chains. Unlike the rare earth export controls extended to January 10, 2027, this ban covers metals critical for night-vision devices, infrared optics, and compound semiconductors, with no near-term substitutes; a lapse without extension would be the most concrete supply-chain shock of the current US-China trade cycle.

headline: USA RARE EARTH DROPS 6% as China Mineral Export Deadline Looms; Critical Metals -5%, MP Materials -3%
snippet: USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ: USAR) fell 6% on November 25 to $6.31 as markets priced in both China's imminent gallium/antimony deadline and the prospect of new US tariffs on critical mineral imports; Critical Metals declined 5% and MP Materials fell 3% in the same session. The sector remains down roughly 40% year-to-date and continues trading as a high-beta play on US-China diplomacy rather than on its own operational fundamentals.

headline: HORIZON GOLD DRILLS 42m AT 2.76 G/T at Gum Creek Kingfisher — Resource Corridor May Extend 90m Further North
snippet: Horizon Gold (ASX: HRN) reported November 26 drill results from the Kingfisher deposit at its Gum Creek gold project in Western Australia, with the best hole returning 42 metres at 2.76 g/t gold; the company says the resource remains open to the north with an interpreted 90-metre extension. A 42-metre intersection at that grade in an open-pittable geometry in WA's established gold belt is the kind of result that moves a small-cap resource estimate into drill-your-own-way territory.

headline: AURIC MINING HITS 9m AT 7.05 G/T FROM 4m DEPTH — Munda Project Near-Surface Gold Delivers Grade in a Sector Selloff
snippet: Auric Mining (ASX: AWJ) released drill results on November 26 from the Munda project, with its best near-surface hole returning 9 metres at 7.05 g/t gold from just 4 metres depth — a shallow, high-grade intercept that reduces strip ratio risk and lowers the threshold for early production economics. Near-surface high-grade results are what small-cap gold investors are looking for in a down market: low capital intensity to first production, strong grade to protect margins if gold weakens further.

headline: AUSTRALIAN GOLD AND COPPER 15m AT 4.0 G/T at Evergreen — Silver, Zinc, Lead Bonuses in Hand; 33 More Holes Permitted
snippet: Australian Gold and Copper (ASX: AGC) reported that hole EGRC019 at the Evergreen project returned 15 metres at 4.0 g/t gold with concurrent silver, zinc, and lead credits on November 26, and that permits for up to 33 additional holes are already in place. The polymetallic payability — gold carries the grade, base metals improve project economics — is a structure that appeals to both gold bulls and battery-metals investors at a time when investors are hunting for projects with built-in revenue diversification.

headline: DLP DOUBLES DOWN IN PERU: Esperanza Grows to 24,900 Ha as Two New Porphyry Copper-Gold Targets Identified
snippet: DLP Resources (TSXV: DLP) expanded its 100%-owned Esperanza copper-gold-molybdenum project in southern Peru to 24,900 hectares and identified two new drill-ready porphyry targets on November 25-26, as the company's maiden drill program — testing the interpreted porphyry core 35 km southwest of Freeport-McMoRan's Cerro Verde mine — advances to its first assay results. Porphyry copper projects of this scale adjacent to Cerro Verde would have been valued in the hundreds of millions at peak cycle; in the current market they are being built cheaply, which is precisely when institutional acquirers tend to notice them.

headline: ALBION RESOURCES 21m AT 1.3 G/T at Gidgee German Well South — WA Junior Extending Resource Footprint in a Down Market
snippet: Albion Resources (ASX: ALB) reported that drill hole ABAC024 at German Well South in the Gidgee Gold project, Western Australia, returned 21 metres at 1.3 g/t gold from 24 metres depth on November 26 — a consistent, mineable intercept that extends the resource to the south. In a capital-constrained market, predictable near-surface mineralisation that extends a known resource is the low-risk drilling story institutional resource funds use to justify retaining small-cap positions through sector downturns.

headline: UBS HOLDS FIRM ON $5,000 GOLD — Bank Says November Selloff Is 'Near-Term Noise,' Structural Bull Thesis Intact for H1 2027
snippet: UBS acknowledged near-term risks in the wake of November's gold selloff — including elevated real yields and a stronger US dollar — but held its $5,000 to $5,200 price target for H1 2027, arguing that the structural drivers of central bank accumulation, de-dollarization, and geopolitical safe-haven demand remain fully intact. The bank's hold-your-nerve message is a direct counter to the multi-broker capitulation seen across Agnico, Barrick, and Newmont this week: for retail investors sitting on gold equity losses, the UBS framing says the thesis hasn't changed, only the entry point has.

headline: GOLDSEEK TECHNICIAN: JUNIOR MINERS SHOW BUY SIGNALS — But Gold Must Break $4,100 Before a Bottom Can Be Called
snippet: David Chapman's weekly Technical Scoop column (Nov 24-25) notes that junior miners are flashing buy signals on the charts — a divergence from still-falling gold prices that sometimes leads by 4-6 weeks — but cautions that gold needs to break and close above $4,100 on a weekly basis before a confirmed bottom can be declared, with $4,500 as the level that would put the low beyond reasonable doubt. The divergence between early junior-miner strength and unconfirmed gold price bottom is a classic pre-reversal pattern, though Chapman notes the Fed rate-hike talk and precious metals divergence from currencies suggest timing remains uncertain.

headline: PRECIOUS METALS SELLOFF WAS FORCED LIQUIDATION — Not Demand Destruction; Physical Buying Surged While Paper Contracts Imploded
snippet: An analysis of November's 12-14% gold and 17% silver rout identifies futures liquidation and leveraged-fund margin calls — not weakening physical demand — as the primary driver, citing a surge in Comex open-interest reduction alongside record physical coin and bar sales at US and European bullion dealers. If forced selling, not demand destruction, caused the rout, the correction has a time-limited floor: once levered longs are flushed, the same structural buyers who drove gold above $4,000 can re-emerge without competing against their own prior positions.
